werk/duane-eddy-have-twangy-guitar-will-.text:
Duane Eddy had already made a few successful singles when his first album was released on 9 January 1958 on Jamie Records. He played with his band The Rebels, whose members included Al Casey on rhythm guitar and Steve Douglas on saxophone. The Sharps provided wordless vocals, with cheering and shouting. Lee Hazlewood and Lester Sill produced.

The record blends early rock and roll with swing, country and blues, and contains both covers and original numbers, such as Rebel Rouser. Five singles released before and after the album reached the Billboard Hot 100. The album itself spent 82 weeks on the charts and peaked at number five. The guide MusicHound Rock calls it one of the cornerstones of modern rock guitar.
werk/duane-eddy-have-twangy-guitar-will-.listen: Listen to how the guitar plays the melody on Rebel Rouser in place of a singer, and notice what the band does around it.

werk/duke-ellington-blues-in-orbit.text:
Duke Ellington recorded Blues in Orbit in 1959 for Columbia. The album was released in 1960. Teo Macero's liner notes describe it above all as a blues record, as most of the titles already suggest. The orchestra includes Johnny Hodges on alto saxophone, Paul Gonsalves on tenor saxophone, Harry Carney on baritone saxophone and Ray Nance on trumpet and violin, among others. Billy Strayhorn plays piano on two tracks. In 2004 the album was reissued on CD, with bonus tracks and alternate takes.

The record lacks the intellectual weight of the suites and concept pieces that attracted so much attention at the time, wrote AllMusic reviewer Bruce Eder. Even so, it is well worth hearing, because here the orchestra shows its lighter side. According to him, it sounds like a late-night session that was half jam, half formal studio recording. Familiar titles such as C Jam Blues and In a Mellow Tone appear alongside new pieces.
werk/duke-ellington-blues-in-orbit.listen: Listen to C Jam Blues and notice how the horns and rhythm section keep hold of the loose, bluesy feel of the record.

werk/duke-ellington-side-by-side.text:
Side by Side is billed as an album by Duke Ellington and Johnny Hodges, but in reality it is Hodges, for many years the alto saxophonist in Ellington's orchestra, who leads. Ellington plays on only three tracks. The rest was recorded in August 1958, with Billy Strayhorn at the piano. The record follows Back to Back, on which the two had played the blues.

Hodges is always in front, surrounded by great names from jazz: Ben Webster, Roy Eldridge, Harry Edison and the drummer Jo Jones. The material ranges from Stompy Jones and Squeeze Me to short, relaxed pieces such as Ruint and Bend One. The album has remained available ever since its release.
werk/duke-ellington-side-by-side.listen: Listen in Stompy Jones to how Hodges's alto saxophone leads the melody and how the other soloists then take the floor in turn.

werk/duncan-laurence-arcade.text: On 18 May 2019 Duncan Laurence won the Eurovision Song Contest in Tel Aviv with Arcade, the first Dutch victory since 1975. Two years later the song became popular again through TikTok, this time outside Europe too. It entered the American charts in 2021 and became one of the most streamed Eurovision songs ever. In 2020 the Netherlands was due to host the contest, but it was cancelled because of the coronavirus pandemic.
werk/duncan-laurence-arcade.listen: Arcade begins with only a piano and a soft voice. Hear how the chorus keeps growing, with a choir in the background.

werk/duran-duran-notorious.text:
Notorious was released on 24 November 1986 and sounded different from Duran Duran's earlier records. The band made the album with producer Nile Rodgers of Chic, and the sound became funkier. Drummer Roger Taylor and guitarist Andy Taylor had already left by the time of its release. Singer Simon Le Bon, keyboard player Nick Rhodes and bassist John Taylor remained as a trio. Guitarist Warren Cuccurullo joined during the mixing and played on a few tracks, and drummer Steve Ferrone also played on the album.

The title track was a great success: number seven in the UK and number two in the United States. The album sold less than earlier records. Critics were divided, although some praised the band's growing maturity and the production.
werk/duran-duran-notorious.listen: Listen in Skin Trade to Nile Rodgers's slim guitar and the soulful vocals. Notice how funky it sounds for a group that became famous with synth-pop.

werk/duran-duran-rio.text:
After their 1981 debut and the hit Girls on Film, Duran Duran wrote the follow-up in a nightclub in Birmingham and in a remote château in France. EMI doubled the budget. Recording took place from January to March 1982 at AIR Studios in London, with producer Colin Thurston. Bassist John Taylor came up with the title.

The band experimented more than before, with vibraphone, marimba and even the sound of a lit cigarette and cracking ice cubes. Rio is new wave and synth-pop with influences from disco and funk. Saxophonist Andy Hamilton played the solo on the title track. The Chauffeur came about on the spot in the studio and is entirely electronic. The cover, painted by Patrick Nagel, is regarded as one of the best ever. The videos helped set off the MTV revolution. Reviews were at first mixed; later the record gained a reputation as timeless and as the band's best work.
werk/duran-duran-rio.listen: Listen to The Chauffeur and notice the electronic sounds: the track was conceived in the studio and contains the sound of a cracking ice cube.

werk/duran-duran-seven-and-the-ragged-ti.text:
Seven and the Ragged Tiger is Duran Duran's third studio album and was released on 21 November 1983. After the success of Rio, the band lived outside Britain for a year to avoid paying tax. Recording ran from April to October 1983 in France, the Caribbean and Australia, with Alex Sadkin, Ian Little and the band as producers. The sessions went badly: there was little new material and tensions in the group were rising.

It is a new wave and synth-pop record in which synthesizers set the tone. Singer Simon Le Bon described the album as an adventure story about a small commando team. It yielded three singles: Union of the Snake, New Moon on Monday and a remix of The Reflex by Nile Rodgers, which reached number one in Britain and the United States. Critics were at first unkind, but the album was a great success and was the last studio record with the original line-up until 2004.
werk/duran-duran-seven-and-the-ragged-ti.listen: Listen to The Reflex and notice how the synthesizers and the rhythm together create the drive of the song.

werk/dusty-springfield-a-girl-called-dus.text:
Dusty Springfield first sang in the Lana Sisters and then in The Springfields, together with her brother Tom. On tour in America she heard soul, and in 1963 she decided to go solo, because she wanted to sing more than the group allowed. Her first single, I Only Want to Be with You, was still recorded with The Springfields. That success led to A Girl Called Dusty, released on 17 April 1964 on Philips. Johnny Franz and the singer herself produced, and Ivor Raymonde conducted the orchestra.

The record contains mostly straightforward pop songs and a few numbers with a Motown influence, such as Mockingbird. For the first time she recorded songs by Burt Bacharach and Hal David and by Gerry Goffin and Carole King. In 1997 the NME called it a fairly strong debut.
werk/dusty-springfield-a-girl-called-dus.listen: Listen to Mockingbird for the Motown influence in the rhythm and in the way she sings.

werk/dusty-springfield-dusty-in-memphis.text:
To breathe new life into her career, Dusty Springfield signed with Atlantic Records, the label of her soul idol Aretha Franklin. The condition was that she work with producer Jerry Wexler. Together they chose eleven songs, mostly pop numbers, which were recorded in the Southern soul style. The first sessions took place at American Sound Studio in Memphis, with the Sweet Inspirations and the studio musicians known as the Memphis Boys. Her vocals and the orchestral parts followed later in New York.

The work was not easy. Springfield had doubts, partly out of fear of being compared with the great soul singers who had worked in the same studio. Son of a Preacher Man became the best-known track; Breakfast in Bed also comes close to Southern soul. The album initially sold poorly but grew into her best-known work. In 2001 it entered the Grammy Hall of Fame, and in 2020 the National Recording Registry.
werk/dusty-springfield-dusty-in-memphis.listen: Listen in Son of a Preacher Man to the supple, rhythmic accompaniment and to how relaxed the vocals sound.

werk/dusty-springfield-ev-rything-s-comi.text:
Ev'rything's Coming Up Dusty is Dusty Springfield's second studio album and was released in 1965 on Philips. Her 1964 debut A Girl Called Dusty had made her the label's best-selling female artist. For that reason this album was given a gatefold sleeve and extensive liner notes.

It mixes ordinary pop songs with show tunes, such as Who Can I Turn To? (When Nobody Needs Me), and with the soul for which she later became known. Doodlin' and That's How Heartaches Are Made had been minor hits for Baby Washington, one of her favourite singers. La Bamba was a popular concert number but does not really fit with the rest. The album reached number 6 in Britain. In the United States it was released under a different title, You Don't Have to Say You Love Me, with the big hit added.
werk/dusty-springfield-ev-rything-s-comi.listen: Listen to That's How Heartaches Are Made, a soul song that was earlier a modest hit for Baby Washington, and notice how she gives it a sound of her own.

werk/dusty-springfield-stay-awhile-i-onl.text:
This was Dusty Springfield's first album in America, released in 1964 by the American arm of Philips. About three months earlier her debut A Girl Called Dusty had come out in England. The American record was in effect a compilation: tracks from that album, her first two singles and other work. The American company preferred to put the hits on an album, such as I Only Want to Be with You, Stay Awhile and Wishin' and Hopin'.

Her next four American records were also assembled in this way. That is said to have contributed to her leaving Philips in America in 1968 and choosing Atlantic. Some fans therefore do not count these records among her real albums, but they do appear in her official discography.
werk/dusty-springfield-stay-awhile-i-onl.listen: Listen to I Only Want To Be With You, the song with which her solo career began, and compare its tone with the later Mockingbird.

werk/eagles-desperado.text:
Desperado is the Eagles' second album and was released on 17 April 1973 on Asylum Records. Glyn Johns produced it again, this time at Island Studios in London. After the success of the first record Glenn Frey wanted to be taken seriously and came up with a concept album. Jackson Browne showed the group a book about Wild West bandits, and from it Doolin-Dalton emerged. The theme became the Wild West, with the outlaw serving as an image for life in rock 'n' roll.

Frey and Henley began writing together after the first record. Desperado and Tequila Sunrise came about in the first week. The title song was never released as a single but became one of the group's best-known songs. Tequila Sunrise and Outlaw Man were the singles. In 2000 the record entered the Grammy Hall of Fame.
werk/eagles-desperado.listen: Listen to Desperado and notice how the lyrics sketch a lonely outlaw.

werk/eagles-eagles.text:
The Eagles' debut album was released on 1 June 1972 on Asylum Records. David Geffen had sent the new band to Aspen to develop, and Glenn Frey wanted Glyn Johns as producer. Johns had doubts after a messy performance, but changed his mind when the four members sang together on Take the Devil. At Olympic Studios in London they recorded the album in two weeks.

Johns emphasised harmonies and an acoustic sound, to the annoyance of Frey and Don Henley, who would have preferred a rougher sound. On Take It Easy, Bernie Leadon plays banjo at double speed. Nightingale was added later in Los Angeles because Henley needed more vocals. Take It Easy, Witchy Woman and Peaceful Easy Feeling all became singles in the American top forty. The album contributed to the rise of country rock.
werk/eagles-eagles.listen: Listen to Take It Easy and notice Bernie Leadon's banjo, which makes the song quick and light.

werk/eagles-hotel-california.text:
The Eagles began writing and recording in March 1976, under producer Bill Szymczyk at Criteria and Record Plant studios. Bernie Leadon, the band's main country influence, had left and been replaced by Joe Walsh. The group deliberately chose a straightforward rock sound, as in Victim of Love and Life in the Fast Lane, for which Walsh supplied the opening riff. The first song to be finished, the title track, became the theme of the record.

Don Henley called the record a concept album: California as a miniature of America as a whole, with themes such as lost innocence and the dark side of the American dream. It was the last album with bassist Randy Meisner. It went straight to the top of the American chart, and Hotel California won a Grammy for Record of the Year.
werk/eagles-hotel-california.listen: Listen to Hotel California and notice how the lyrics tell their story like a film, as Glenn Frey intended.

werk/eagles-on-the-border.text:
On their third album the band wanted a more robust rock sound than the country rock of the first two records. It began with producer Glyn Johns at Olympic Studios in London, but the group felt he emphasised their country sound too much. They returned to California and continued with Bill Szymczyk, in Miami and Los Angeles. Guitarist Don Felder, an old friend of Bernie Leadon, played slide guitar on Good Day in Hell.

The three singles were Already Gone, James Dean and The Best of My Love, the band's first number one. On My Man, Leadon commemorates his friends Duane Allman and Gram Parsons. Critics saw the record as a transitional work that looked back to earlier work and ahead to what was still to come.
werk/eagles-on-the-border.listen: Listen to Ol' 55 and notice how Glenn Frey and Don Henley share the singing: what changes in the song when the voice switches?

werk/eagles-one-of-these-nights.text:
At the end of 1974 the band began work on their fourth album. Many songs came about in the house in Beverly Hills that Glenn Frey and Don Henley shared, including One of These Nights, Lyin' Eyes and Take It to the Limit. Frey called it the smoothest and most painless record they ever made. Even so, discontent grew in Bernie Leadon, who did not want to follow Frey's rock direction. It was the last album with the original line-up; Joe Walsh took his place afterwards.

The record was the commercial breakthrough: it reached number one in the United States and yielded three top-ten singles. Randy Meisner sings Take It to the Limit, and on Visions Don Felder sings the lead part, the only time he does so.
werk/eagles-one-of-these-nights.listen: Listen to Bernie Leadon's Journey of the Sorcerer and notice how bluegrass and psychedelia come together in a single song.

werk/earth-wind-en-fire-head-to-the-sky.text:
Head to the Sky was released in May 1973 as Earth, Wind & Fire's fourth album. Joe Wissert produced it, with bandleader Maurice White as musical director. It was recorded at Clover Recorders in Hollywood. Besides guitars, organ and piano, a sitar, a clarinet and a kalimba can be heard. On Zanzibar, guest musician Oscar Brashear plays trumpet.

The album mixes soul, funk and jazz. Evil became a modest hit and Keep Your Head to the Sky also reached the soul chart. The newspaper Pittsburgh Press noticed Jessica Cleaves's soft vocals, and Billboard thought the band did everything well. The album reached number 2 on the Billboard Top Soul Albums chart and later went platinum. According to AllMusic the group still had mainly a cult following, but that changed, and when success came in 1974 and 1975, new fans discovered how good this record already was. Isaac Hayes called it one of their five essential records.
werk/earth-wind-en-fire-head-to-the-sky.listen: Listen to Zanzibar and notice the long, calm instrumental atmosphere of this closing track: which wind instruments do you hear playing solos?

werk/earth-wind-en-fire-last-days-and-ti.text:
Last Days and Time is Earth, Wind & Fire's third album and their first for Columbia. It was released in October 1972. Joe Wissert produced it at Sunset Sound Studios in Hollywood. Maurice White played drums and kalimba, Verdine White bass, and Philip Bailey sang and played congas. Ronnie Laws played flute and saxophone.

The record is full of covers: Make It with You by Bread and Where Have All the Flowers Gone by Pete Seeger. Between them come short interludes. The album sounds eclectic and mixes soul, funk, pop and jazzy experiments. William Ruhlmann of AllMusic wrote that here the group had recorded almost everything that Motown, Sly & the Family Stone and Weather Report had done. The single Mom reached number 39 on the Cashbox R&B chart. Producer Jimmy Jam became a fan of the group through this album, and Nas drew inspiration from the cover.
werk/earth-wind-en-fire-last-days-and-ti.listen: Listen to Where Have All the Flowers Gone and notice how a 1960s folk song takes on a soul sound here through Philip Bailey's singing and the band.

werk/earth-wind-en-fire-that-s-the-way-o.text:
That's the Way of the World was released on 3 March 1975 on Columbia Records and was at the same time the soundtrack of a film of the same name. It was Earth, Wind & Fire's sixth studio album. Bandleader Maurice White produced it together with Charles Stepney, and the recording and mixing took nine months.

The album brings together funk, African influences, jazz and gentle ballads. Shining Star reached number 1 on the American singles chart and won a Grammy. The title song also did well on the charts, and on Africano you can hear what the African side of the group sounds like. The album spent three weeks at the top of the Billboard 200 and in 2004 was given a place in the Grammy Hall of Fame. One reviewer called it a short, focused record on which White brought together all the elements of the group.
werk/earth-wind-en-fire-that-s-the-way-o.listen: Listen to Shining Star and notice how the singing of several voices together forms a big, clear sound.

werk/earth-wind-en-fire-the-need-of-love.text:
The Need of Love is Earth, Wind & Fire's second studio album and was released in November 1971 on Warner Bros. Records. Joe Wissert produced the record, which was recorded at Sunset Sound Studios in Hollywood. It became the group's last album for Warner Bros. until Millennium in 1993. Jean Carne was among those who sang along, and Everything Is Everything is an adaptation of the Donny Hathaway song.

The nine-piece band mixes jazzy instrumental pieces with group singing and chanting, big band sounds, free passages and solid soul rhythms. According to the Chicago Sun-Times critic this sounds melodic and enchanting, and the mixture has a sound of its own. AllMusic found the record more abstract in design than the debut, but with fewer good songs. Billboard already saw potential in the group behind the singer Sherry Scott. I Think About Lovin' You reached number 44 on the soul chart.
werk/earth-wind-en-fire-the-need-of-love.listen: Listen to Everything Is Everything and notice how the band turns a Donny Hathaway song into a version of its own.

werk/eberhard-weber-the-colours-of-chloe.text:
The Colours of Chloë is the debut of the German double bassist and composer Eberhard Weber. He recorded the album in December 1973 and it was released a year later on ECM. On the record Weber plays not only bass but also cello, ocarina and voice. He works with the pianist and synthesizer player Rainer Brüninghaus, drummer Peter Giger, flugelhorn player Ack van Rooyen, singer Gisela Schäuble and the cellos of the Südfunk Orchestra of Stuttgart.

AllMusic calls the album Weber's best-known and most influential work, an ambitious piece of symphonic jazz that helped define the ECM sound: painterly, romantic, at times rhythmically animated and at times minimalist. Opinions differ on whether the record has stood the test of time, but Weber's aesthetic played an important role in the creative music of the 1970s and attracted many followers.
werk/eberhard-weber-the-colours-of-chloe.listen: Listen to The Colours Of Chloë and try to hear how the double bass, the strings and the voice together form a painterly whole.

werk/eddie-harris-cool-sax-warm-heart.text:
Saxophonist Eddie Harris recorded this album in 1964 for Columbia. Tom Wilson was the producer. Harris plays tenor saxophone, with Wynton Kelly on piano on four tracks, Warren Stephens on guitar, Melvin Jackson on bass and Bucky Taylor on drums. The Malcom Dodds Singers sing along, and a few other musicians whose names are not known also play.

The programme combines Harris's own pieces, such as Chicago Serenade and Brother Ed, with standards by Gershwin and Buddy Johnson and a number by Django Reinhardt. At just over seven minutes, Brother Ed is the longest track. The reception was mixed. AllMusic called the record pleasant at some moments but found it largely run-of-the-mill and advised listening to his work for Atlantic instead. As a result the album is overshadowed by the records for which Harris became best known.
werk/eddie-harris-cool-sax-warm-heart.listen: Listen to Brother Ed, the longest track, and notice how Harris lets his tenor saxophone breathe during the solo.

werk/eddie-harris-exodus-to-jazz.text:
Eddie Harris recorded his debut album in 1961 for the label Vee-Jay. He plays tenor sax in a quintet with, among others, pianist Willie Pickens and guitarist Joe Diorio. He wrote four of the eight tracks himself.

The title refers to Exodus, Ernest Gold's film music, which Harris brings into a new jazz form. AllMusic calls the record full of concise, smoothly swinging tracks. His tone is cool and close to Stan Getz, with here and there a touch of soul jazz. This made the record a forerunner of much crossover success in the 1960s, although it is still far from his later, funkier work.
werk/eddie-harris-exodus-to-jazz.listen: Listen in Exodus to how Harris plays the familiar film melody in a jazz form of his own, with a cool tone on the tenor sax.

werk/eddie-harris-jazz-for-breakfast-at-.text:
This third album by Eddie Harris, from 1961, was released on Vee-Jay. It is a jazz adaptation of the music Henry Mancini wrote for the film Breakfast at Tiffany's. Harris plays tenor sax, accompanied by trombone, vibraphone, piano, guitar, bass and drums.

The record follows the film music, from Moon River to The Big Heist, and keeps Mancini's melodies. AllMusic observes that Harris has many fresh ideas but never strays far from the melody. In this way a film score is turned into short jazz numbers in which the saxophone takes the leading role. Many tracks last only two or three minutes; only Moon River and the title song run to about five minutes.
werk/eddie-harris-jazz-for-breakfast-at-.listen: Listen in Moon River to how Harris keeps Mancini's melody recognisable and yet gives it a colour of his own.

werk/eddie-harris-mighty-like-a-rose.text:
Mighty Like a Rose is saxophonist Eddie Harris's second album. He recorded it in 1961 for the label Vee-Jay. He plays tenor saxophone in a quintet with Willie Pickens on piano, Joe Diorio on guitar, Bill Yancey on bass and Harold Jones on drums.

The repertoire consists of standards such as My Buddy and Willow Weep for Me, the film theme Spartacus by Alex North and God Bless the Child by Billie Holiday. There is also a piece by John Lewis and two original numbers by Harris. His playing seeks a balance between cool bop and outright soul-jazz. You can already hear something of the influence of Yusef Lateef, a musician from Detroit. According to AllMusic everything is well executed and Harris beautifully commands the highest registers of his instrument. That makes the album worthwhile for anyone who liked Exodus to Jazz.
werk/eddie-harris-mighty-like-a-rose.listen: Listen to God Bless the Child and notice how Harris makes the melody sing on his saxophone.

werk/einsturzende-neubauten-halber-mensc.text:
Halber Mensch is the third album by the German industrial band Einstürzende Neubauten and was released on 2 September 1985. Here the group shows a broader artistic range. Yü-Gung (Fütter mein Ego) contains elements of electronic dance music, and the title track is almost a cappella.

The dynamics are also greater. In Seele Brennt, Blixa Bargeld's voice suddenly leaps from a barely audible whisper to a high scream. In Letztes Biest (am Himmel), calm bass guitar notes float above modest percussion. Trouser Press called it their strongest record and AllMusic an outstanding achievement of industrial music. In 2019 Pitchfork ranked it second among the best industrial albums of all time.
werk/einsturzende-neubauten-halber-mensc.listen: Listen to Seele Brennt and notice the moment when the whisper turns into a scream.

werk/einsturzende-neubauten-haus-der-lug.text:
Haus der Lüge is the fifth studio album by the German group Einstürzende Neubauten. It was released in 1989 on Rough Trade Records and later reissued by Some Bizzare in England, by the band's own label Potomak in Europe and by Thirsty Ear in the United States. The five band members are Blixa Bargeld, Mark Chung, Alexander Hacke, N.U. Unruh and F.M. Einheit. Bargeld sings and plays guitar, Hacke also plays guitar, Chung plays bass, and Unruh and Einheit beat on percussion.

The album opens with Prolog and Feurio!, followed by Fiat Lux and Der Kuss, among others. Fiat Lux lasts well over twelve minutes and consists of three parts. In the part Maifestspiele we hear recordings the group made at a demonstration in Kreuzberg in Berlin on 1 May 1987. Critics were positive. Trouser Press thought it a much stronger album than Fünf, and Ned Raggett of AllMusic wrote that the group closed the decade at a peak.
werk/einsturzende-neubauten-haus-der-lug.listen: Listen to Fiat Lux and notice the part Maifestspiele: can you hear how the recordings of the demonstration in Kreuzberg are set among the group's music?

werk/einsturzende-neubauten-kollaps.text:
Kollaps is Einstürzende Neubauten's first official album, released in 1981 on the German label ZickZack. Blixa Bargeld, N.U. Unruh and F.M. Einheit play on it. The tracks combine raw punk with industrial sounds from home-built musical machines, electronics and found objects such as metal sheets. Jet'm is a cover of the song by Serge Gainsbourg, Je t'aime... moi non plus. Many CD versions add tracks, including a 1987 live recording of Negativ Nein, and the 2002 reissue also contains the Stahldubversions from 1982.

Trouser Press called Kollaps one of the most shocking visions ever committed to vinyl. The album is also included in the book 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die.
werk/einsturzende-neubauten-kollaps.listen: Listen to Kollaps, at over eight minutes the longest track, and notice the industrial sounds alongside the voice.

werk/einsturzende-neubauten-zeichnungen-.text:
Zeichnungen des Patienten O. T. is Einstürzende Neubauten's second studio album, released in 1983 by Some Bizzare Records and distributed in Germany by Rough Trade Deutschland. In the United States it was released in 1984 as Drawings of O. T. The title refers to Oswald Tschirtner, an artist with schizophrenia who lived in an institution and became known for his drawings.

The album shows more moods and sounds than the debut Kollaps. Besides the metallic clatter of hitting, scraping and plucking, the group uses found sounds, such as telephone conversations and the Hamburg fish market, and early forms of sampling. The bass guitar is conspicuously present but modestly played. Armenia features a sampled Armenian song, and the piece was later used in films by Michael Mann. The critic David Sheridan observed that the group was tending towards the conventional: the title song even has a chord progression.
werk/einsturzende-neubauten-zeichnungen-.listen: Listen to Armenia and notice the sampled Armenian song in the track.

werk/electric-light-orchestra-face-the-m.text:
Face the Music, the band's fifth album, was released in September 1975. Jeff Lynne, the sole songwriter, wanted to move from the large-scale classical sound of Eldorado towards more recognisable pop songs, although the strings remained prominent. Bassist Kelly Groucutt and cellist Melvyn Gale replaced two departed members. Recording began at Musicland Studios in Munich, on the advice of Deep Purple. The orchestra was recorded separately in London. It became the group's first album to go platinum.

Lynne wrote Evil Woman in a few minutes, near the end of the sessions, as filler. It became a worldwide hit. Fire on High opens with synthesizer and choir and contains a backwards message, spoken by drummer Bev Bevan, as a joke by Lynne. In Nightrider, Lynne and Groucutt take turns singing lead, and at the end the backing singers imitate strings.
werk/electric-light-orchestra-face-the-m.listen: Listen to the beginning of Fire on High: a synthesizer plays a repeating chord with a choir, and in between a backwards spoken message can be heard.

werk/electric-light-orchestra-on-the-thi.text:
On the Third Day is Electric Light Orchestra's third album and the first without Roy Wood. It was released in November 1973 in America and on 14 December 1973 in England. From this record onwards the word The disappeared from the band's name. The four tracks on the first side run into one another as one continuous suite, and the songs are shorter than on the previous record. The second side was recorded during or shortly after the sessions for ELO 2.

Violinist Mik Kaminski made his debut on the first side, replacing Wilfred Gibson. Marc Bolan plays as a second lead guitarist. The album did not chart in England but reached number 52 in America. The American cover was a photograph by Richard Avedon in which the band members show their navels.
werk/electric-light-orchestra-on-the-thi.listen: Listen to Ma-Ma-Ma Belle for the guitar of guest musician Marc Bolan, who plays here as second lead guitarist.

werk/electric-light-orchestra-out-of-the.text:
Jeff Lynne wrote this entire double album in three and a half weeks, after withdrawing to a rented chalet in the Swiss Alps. Recording in Munich took another two months. It was Electric Light Orchestra's seventh studio album, and Lynne wrote and produced everything himself.

The record was one of the first pop albums to make extensive use of the vocoder. The third side is a suite about the weather, Concerto for a Rainy Day, inspired by the endless rain in Switzerland. Rain and thunder sound between the tracks. The suite ends with Mr. Blue Sky, which Lynne wrote on the day the sun finally broke through after bad weather. A blow on a fire extinguisher produces the bell-like sound in the performance. Worldwide, about ten million copies were sold.
werk/electric-light-orchestra-out-of-the.listen: Listen to the end of Mr. Blue Sky, where a vocoder sings a message to whoever is playing the record. What does that voice ask?

werk/elis-regina-poema-de-amor.text:
Poema de Amor is the second album by the Brazilian singer Elis Regina and was released in 1962. It was her last record for the label Continental, because around that time she signed with Copacabana. Recording was already under way on 21 January 1962, with arrangements by Renato de Oliveira.

The record has twelve songs. A large part are Portuguese adaptations of foreign songs, such as Meu Pequeno Mundo De Ilusão, which goes back to a song by Bob Hilliard and Lee Pockriss. There are also Brazilian songs, such as the title song Poema by Fernando Dias and Pororó-Popó by João Roberto Kelly.
werk/elis-regina-poema-de-amor.listen: Listen to Meu Pequeno Mundo De Ilusão to hear how the song sounds in Portuguese, and compare it with My Little Corner of the World if you know it.

werk/ella-fitzgerald-ella-fitzgerald-sin.text:
This 1956 double album was Ella Fitzgerald's first for the new label Verve, and the first that Verve released. Manager and producer Norman Granz wanted to make her more than a singer for jazz lovers. He therefore chose a songbook of numbers by Cole Porter, with a studio orchestra conducted by Buddy Bregman. The accompaniment had to change just enough to let jazz show through here and there. The recording took place in February and March 1956 in Hollywood.

It became the start of a series of eight songbook albums, each devoted to a different composer from the Great American Songbook. Granz played the whole record to Porter, who merely remarked on how good the singer's diction was. In 2000 the album entered the Grammy Hall of Fame and in 2003 the Library of Congress chose it for the National Recording Registry.
werk/ella-fitzgerald-ella-fitzgerald-sin.listen: Listen to her diction on Anything Goes: every word can be understood, and it was precisely this that Porter himself pointed out.

werk/ella-fitzgerald-lullabies-of-birdla.text:
Lullabies of Birdland, from 1955, is not a record made in a single go. Decca gathered tracks from the late 1940s and early 1950s that had previously appeared on 78 rpm singles. Ella Fitzgerald sings them each with a different accompaniment: Sy Oliver's orchestra, Ray Brown's trio, Hank Jones's quartet and Bob Haggart's orchestra.

The record contains standards such as Angel Eyes, How High the Moon, Basin Street Blues and Oh Lady Be Good, besides Lullaby of Birdland, George Shearing's title song. Ella Hums the Blues is the singer's own composition. In 1998 MCA released the whole album on CD, together with Sweet and Hot from the same year.
werk/ella-fitzgerald-lullabies-of-birdla.listen: Listen to How High the Moon and notice how the singer's voice carries this standard.

werk/elliott-smith-either-or.text:
Elliott Smith recorded his third album in 1995 and 1996, at several locations, mainly in Portland, while he was still a member of Heatmiser. He made it with producers Tom Rothrock and Rob Schnapf and released it in 1997 on Kill Rock Stars, after Heatmiser had split up. The title comes from a book by Søren Kierkegaard. Places in Portland turn up in the lyrics, such as the Alameda neighbourhood and Division Street.

The sound forms a bridge between the sombre lo-fi of his first records and the smoother studio sound of later albums. One reviewer heard more clarity and pop feeling in it than on the acoustic confessions of the previous album. The record did not reach the American charts, but critics were full of praise. Director Gus Van Sant used Between the Bars, Angeles and Say Yes in the film Good Will Hunting, and as a result Smith was briefly in the spotlight.
werk/elliott-smith-either-or.listen: Listen to Between the Bars and notice how little is needed: a soft, intimate recording in which mainly voice and guitar can be heard.

werk/elliott-smith-figure-8.text:
This fifth album by Elliott Smith was released on 18 April 2000 and was his second on a major label, DreamWorks. Recording ran from 1998 to 2000 and took place in several studios, including Sunset Sound in Hollywood and Abbey Road in London. At first the record was to be called Place Pigalle. Of the eventual title Smith said that he liked the image of a skater in an endless, winding circle: it is not about arriving, but about making something as beautiful as possible.

He described the songs as more fragmented and dreamy. The lyrics refer to, among others, the serial killer David Berkowitz, the Hindu god Shiva and the actor Bruno Schleinstein. Happiness and Son of Sam preceded the album as singles. Critics described the sound as layered power pop with intimate ballads. The album received much praise, although some reviewers found it weaker than XO. It remained his last album in his lifetime.
werk/elliott-smith-figure-8.listen: Listen to Happiness and notice the unusually cheerful energy in the production for a writer who often sounds restrained.

werk/elton-john-empty-sky.text:
Empty Sky was Elton John's debut and was released on 6 June 1969 in the United Kingdom. The album was recorded in the winter of 1968 and the spring of 1969 in the eight-track studio of DJM Records. It is the only album from his early period not produced by Gus Dudgeon: that was done by Steve Brown, a DJM employee. In the United States the record was not released until January 1975.

John himself plays piano, organ and harpsichord, with guitarist Caleb Quaye and drummer Roger Pope, among others. Skyline Pigeon is the best-known song, one of the first songs about which he and lyricist Bernie Taupin became truly enthusiastic. Later he recorded it again, with orchestra and piano in place of harpsichord. A reviewer of the time found the lyrics still somewhat pretentious, but the music beautiful. In retrospect AllMusic saw mainly promise in it. He himself calls the album naive.
werk/elton-john-empty-sky.listen: Listen to Skyline Pigeon and notice the harpsichord that takes the place of the piano here. If you know the later version, compare it with the recording with orchestra.

werk/elton-john-goodbye-yellow-brick-roa.text:
It began with a plan to record in Jamaica. Problems with the sound system and the studio piano, a boxing match in Kingston and political unrest made the band leave before anything usable was on tape. In 1973 the record was made in two weeks at the Château d'Hérouville in France, where Elton John had worked before. Bernie Taupin wrote the lyrics in about two and a half weeks. Producer Gus Dudgeon had not planned a double album, but there were enough songs.

Through cinematic images the record builds a longing for a childhood that is over. On it you find Bennie and the Jets, Candle in the Wind, a tribute to Marilyn Monroe, and the eleven-minute Funeral for a Friend / Love Lies Bleeding. The album spent eight weeks at number one in the United States, was given a place in the Grammy Hall of Fame in 2003 and is regarded as one of his best.
werk/elton-john-goodbye-yellow-brick-roa.listen: Listen to Funeral for a Friend / Love Lies Bleeding and notice how generously the record opens: with a piece of about eleven minutes, made up of two titles that together form a single whole.

werk/elton-john-madman-across-the-water.text:
Madman Across the Water was released on 5 November 1971 and was Elton John's third album of that year. Bernie Taupin wrote the lyrics. His own band played on only one track, because producer Gus Dudgeon did not trust the group for studio work. In their place came studio musicians and string arrangements by Paul Buckmaster. Davey Johnstone played guitar and Rick Wakeman of Yes played Hammond organ on two tracks.

The title song was first intended for Tumbleweed Connection but was re-recorded. Singles were Levon and Tiny Dancer. In the United Kingdom the record did modestly, at number 41, but in North America it did much better. Rolling Stone found the lyrics confusing and the record at times impenetrably dense.
werk/elton-john-madman-across-the-water.listen: Listen to Tiny Dancer and notice the interplay of piano, vocals and strings.

werk/elvin-jones-and-then-again.text:
And Then Again is a jazz album by drummer Elvin Jones from 1965, released on the label Atlantic. He plays in a sextet with his brothers Thad on cornet and Hank on piano, together with trombonist J.J. Johnson, baritone saxophonist Charles Davis and bassist Art Davis. On three tracks pianist Don Friedman and bassist Paul Chambers take the places of Hank and Art, and saxophonist Frank Wess joins.

Melba Liston arranged and conducted six of the seven tracks and wrote three of them herself: All Deliberate Speed, Elvin Elpus and Len Sirrah. The other pieces are by Charles Davis, Jodora Marshall, Thad Jones and the drummer himself, who wrote the title track.
werk/elvin-jones-and-then-again.listen: Listen in All Deliberate Speed to Melba Liston's arrangements and to how the horns sound together.

werk/elvin-jones-dear-john-c.text:
Dear John C. is an album by drummer Elvin Jones, recorded in February 1965 for the label Impulse!. By John C. in the title he means John Coltrane, with whom he had played earlier. Jones leads a quartet here with alto saxophonist Charlie Mariano, pianist Roland Hanna and bassist Richard Davis. On three tracks Hank Jones plays piano.

The repertoire is varied and includes Love Bird by Charles Mingus, Anthropology by Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker, and Feeling Good and Fantazm by Duke Ellington. According to AllMusic nothing is overdone, not even in Jones's own drumming. The album displays teamwork and restrained dynamics and, according to that review, is too often underestimated. The reviewer finds it worthwhile for drummers and jazz lovers to listen to it again.
werk/elvin-jones-dear-john-c.listen: Listen to Dear John C. and notice how Elvin Jones accompanies without dominating: how does the drumming keep supporting the saxophone?

werk/elvin-jones-elvin.text:
Elvin! is a jazz album by drummer Elvin Jones, recorded in 1961 and 1962 and released on the label Riverside. Here he plays in a group with his brothers, Thad on cornet and Hank on piano, together with tenor saxophonist Frank Foster, flautist Frank Wess and bassist Art Davis.

The material is largely little known: only You Are Too Beautiful is a true standard. Many pieces are by Thad Jones, the rest by Oliver Nelson and Ernie Wilkins, among others. AllMusic heard straight-ahead music with a strong Count Basie feel and wrote that the drummer can swing even in such a fairly conventional setting. According to the same review, all the musicians are in good form.
werk/elvin-jones-elvin.listen: Listen in Ray-El, at eight minutes the longest track, to the drumming beneath the soloists.

werk/elvin-jones-midnight-walk.text:
Midnight Walk was recorded in New York in March 1966, over two days, 23 and 24 March, and was released on the label Atlantic. Drummer Elvin Jones leads a quintet with his brother Thad Jones on trumpet, tenor saxophonist Hank Mobley, pianist Dollar Brand and bassist Don Moore. On one of the tracks Stephen James plays electric piano, and on three others George Abend plays percussion.

The repertoire comes from various writers. Arif Mardin wrote the title track, Stephen James wrote Lycra Too?, Dollar Brand contributed Tintiyana and Mobley wrote H.M. On F.M. Thad Jones wrote Cross-Purpose and All of Us, and the leader himself is the composer of The Juggler.
werk/elvin-jones-midnight-walk.listen: Listen to Tintiyana and notice how Dollar Brand's piano relates to the drums.

werk/elvis-costello-king-of-america.text:
King of America came about after Elvis Costello and T Bone Burnett had toured together as the Coward Brothers. Burnett wanted the next record to consist mainly of voice and acoustic guitar. In 1985 Costello recorded the album in Los Angeles with American session musicians, chosen by Burnett and known as the Confederates, among them Ray Brown, Earl Palmer and former members of Elvis Presley's TCB Band. His regular band, the Attractions, plays on only one track, Suit of Lights.

The sound is mainly acoustic and draws its influences from roots rock, country, folk and R&B. The personal songs deal with love, betrayal, alcoholism and the American dream. Don't Let Me Be Misunderstood, a cover of a song by Nina Simone, became a single in the British top 40. Critics saw the record as a return to his best form, and later it came to be regarded as one of his best works.
werk/elvis-costello-king-of-america.listen: Listen to Brilliant Mistake for the acoustic accompaniment and for how personal the lyrics sound.

werk/elvis-costello-my-aim-is-true.text:
Under his real name, Declan MacManus, Elvis Costello had played in clubs and pubs since 1970, without a record contract. In August 1976 he signed with Stiff Records, which gave him a new first name and an image that suited the emerging punk scene. The record was made between late 1976 and early 1977 in six four-hour sessions at Pathway Studios in London, for about 2,000 pounds. Nick Lowe produced. The backing came from the American country rock group Clover, who did not appear on the cover because of contract problems.

The music combines punk, new wave and pub rock with rock and roll, R&B and rockabilly. The lyrics are grim and revolve around revenge and guilt. The first three singles did not chart, but the record itself was praised and reached number fourteen in the United Kingdom.
werk/elvis-costello-my-aim-is-true.listen: Listen to Watching the Detectives and notice how the tense atmosphere and the sharp lyrics carry the song.

werk/elvis-costello-spike.text:
Spike was Elvis Costello's first album for Warner Bros. and the first since My Aim Is True without the Attractions. The producer was T Bone Burnett, who had also produced King of America. Recording took place in four locations: Hollywood, New Orleans, Dublin and London, each with a different group of musicians. He wrote two songs together with Paul McCartney, including Veronica, his biggest American hit.

The lyrics are sharp. Let Him Dangle is a protest song against the death penalty, about the execution of Derek Bentley in 1953. Tramp the Dirt Down is a bitter song about the Thatcher government. The album reached number five in England and came seventh in The Village Voice's Pazz & Jop poll.
werk/elvis-costello-spike.listen: Listen to Stalin Malone: the lyrics are in the booklet, but on the recording the track is instrumental. Notice what you hear as a result.

werk/elvis-costello-the-juliet-letters.text:
Elvis Costello first heard the Brodsky Quartet in 1989, when it played all of Shostakovich's string quartets. In November 1991 they began work on a plan together. The idea was a series of imaginary letters to Juliet Capulet. All five musicians co-wrote the lyrics and the music. No overdubs were used: the whole album was recorded live in the studio. The singer called it not a rock opera but something new, a song cycle for string quartet and voice.

The record was released in 1993 on Warner Bros. Records. AllMusic called it a special, unusual record that combines chamber music with artistic pop. Spin thought it the singer's best excursion outside pop and rock. Ultimate Classic Rock called it ambitious, but also somewhat dull.
werk/elvis-costello-the-juliet-letters.listen: Listen to Jacksons, Monk and Rowe, the album's only single. Notice how the strings and the voice together carry the song.

werk/elvis-presley-his-hand-in-mine.text:
His Hand in Mine was released on 23 November 1960 on RCA Victor. It was the first of three gospel albums that Elvis Presley released in his lifetime. He had loved church music since his youth and often used it to warm up before performances and recording sessions. He had already devoted an EP to gospel, Peace in the Valley, and he was keen to make a full album. That fitted the plans of manager Colonel Tom Parker, who wanted to give him a family-friendly image.

The recording took place on 30 and 31 October 1960 at RCA Studio B in Nashville, and all the tracks were completed in a single fourteen-hour session. On the record we hear The Jordanaires, pianist Floyd Cramer and guitarist Scotty Moore, among others. Surrender and Crying in the Chapel were recorded during the same session but saved for singles. The album reached number 13 on the American chart and later went gold and platinum.
werk/elvis-presley-his-hand-in-mine.listen: Listen to His Hand In Mine and notice the choral singing of The Jordanaires behind the singer. Hear how calm and restrained the accompaniment remains.

werk/elvis-presley-pot-luck.text:
Pot Luck with Elvis is Elvis Presley's seventh studio album and was released on 18 May 1962 on RCA Victor. Recording took place between March 1961 and March 1962, at Radio Recorders in Hollywood and at RCA Studio B in Nashville. The album reached fourth place on the Billboard chart.

The writers Doc Pomus and Mort Shuman supplied most of the songs. Don Robertson, Otis Blackwell and Paul Evans also contributed. That's Someone You Never Forget came from Presley himself, together with Red West, perhaps as a remembrance of his late mother. (Such an) Easy Question was later released as a single. The record made the top ten, but the soundtrack albums G.I. Blues and Blue Hawaii sold far more. After that Presley made no studio album for seven years, until From Elvis in Memphis.
werk/elvis-presley-pot-luck.listen: Listen to That's Someone You Never Forget, the song Presley came up with and helped write himself, and notice the restrained atmosphere.

werk/emerson-lake-en-palmer-brain-salad-.text:
After the tour for Trilogy, Emerson, Lake & Palmer founded their own record label Manticore in 1973 and converted an old cinema in Fulham into a rehearsal space. Brain Salad Surgery was recorded in London from June to September 1973 and released on 7 December. Greg Lake produced, and the cover is by H. R. Giger. The trio wanted a record they could also play live, unlike Trilogy with its many overdubs.

The longest piece is Karn Evil 9, almost thirty minutes in three parts, written by Keith Emerson, with lyrics by Lake and Pete Sinfield, about the struggle between artificial and natural intelligence. Toccata is an adaptation of Ginastera, who gave his approval. Still...You Turn Me On, written by Lake alone, forms the quiet counterweight. The first reactions were mixed, later appraisals more favourable.
werk/emerson-lake-en-palmer-brain-salad-.listen: Listen to Toccata and try to hear the middle section where Carl Palmer plays electronic drum synthesizers.

werk/emerson-lake-en-palmer-emerson-lake.text:
In the spring of 1970 the trio came together, rehearsed and put together material for a first record: a mixture of original songs and rock adaptations of classical music. In July 1970 the group recorded the album at Advision Studios, although it had never yet played live. Singer and bassist Greg Lake produced. The Barbarian is an adaptation of a piano piece by Béla Bartók, and Knife-Edge leans on Leoš Janáček with a long passage by Bach on organ. Lucky Man was written by Lake at the age of twelve on acoustic guitar, and it ends with an improvised Moog solo by Emerson.

The album was released in November 1970 on Island Records and reached number 4 in the United Kingdom. The performance at the Isle of Wight Festival then made the group famous at lightning speed. Critics later called it the group's most musical record.
werk/emerson-lake-en-palmer-emerson-lake.listen: Listen to the end of Lucky Man: how does the Moog solo sound, and what does the gliding tone do to the simple acoustic song before it?

werk/emerson-lake-en-palmer-tarkus.text:
After a tour of Europe the group took their places again in January 1971 at Advision Studios in London. Greg Lake produced and Eddy Offord was again the sound engineer. Keith Emerson wrote the twenty-minute title piece, and when he played it to the others Lake nearly walked out. After a conversation with the managers he stayed, contributed musical ideas and wrote the lyrics. The piece has seven parts and, according to Lake, is about the senselessness of war. The cover shows an armoured monstrosity, half armadillo and half tank. For the second side the group had no material ready, so a series of separate songs in widely differing styles was put together.

Tarkus was released in June 1971 on Island Records and reached number one on the British album chart. It is the only album by the group to do so. In the United States it reached number 9.
werk/emerson-lake-en-palmer-tarkus.listen: Listen to Tarkus and notice the changing time signatures in Eruption: how do drums and keyboards keep hold of each other? At the end of the piece, hear the Moog in Aquatarkus.

werk/eminem-encore.text:
Encore is Sam Cooke's second studio album and was released in 1958 on Keen Records. Bumps Blackwell produced the record and wrote the arrangements. The album fits into a gradual shift towards more elaborate productions of Cooke's songs: on six of the twelve tracks, horns are added.

The record consists of well-known standards, such as When I Fall in Love, My Foolish Heart, I Cover the Waterfront and Ac-cent-tchu-ate the Positive. Cooke is thus not singing his own work, but songs that had long existed. Incidentally, the sleeve gives the wrong composers' names for When I Fall in Love and My Foolish Heart. Both songs were written by Victor Young. On the cover Cooke wears a grey suit and has closely cropped hair.
werk/eminem-encore.listen: Listen in When I Fall in Love to how Cooke sings the melody of this well-known song, and notice how calmly and evenly he does so.

werk/eminem-relapse.text:
Relapse is Eminem's sixth studio album, released on 15 May 2009. It was his first album after a break caused by writer's block and an addiction to sleeping pills. After the death of his friend Proof he ran into trouble again. In 2008, after a rehab programme, he began recording again. Dr. Dre produced all the tracks except Beautiful, which Eminem made himself.

It is a horrorcore concept album about rehab and relapse, on which his alter ego Slim Shady returns. He plays a serial killer with a variety of accents, and short sketches feature Dominic West, among others. Crack a Bottle reached number one on the American Hot 100. Reviews were mixed, but the record won a Grammy for Best Rap Album and is now often rated more highly.
werk/eminem-relapse.listen: Listen to 3 A.M. and notice how the rapper presents himself as a serial killer and how the accents colour the story.

werk/eminem-the-eminem-show.text:
On 26 May 2002 Eminem's fourth album was released. He produced most of it himself. Dr. Dre was executive producer and made three tracks, and Jeff Bass worked on the later singles. The title comes from the film The Truman Show: his life felt like a circus in which he was always being watched.

After two albums about the frustration of the American underclass, the tone here is more personal. The lyrics deal with fame, his family and the United States after 9/11. There is also more rock than before. Sing for the Moment uses a sample of Dream On by Aerosmith, and the beat of 'Till I Collapse leans on the intro of We Will Rock You by Queen. Critics praised the mature, introspective lyrics and the experimental productions. Several magazines named it the best album of 2002, and it won a Grammy for Best Rap Album.
werk/eminem-the-eminem-show.listen: Listen to 'Till I Collapse and notice the beat: the stomp and clap come from the intro of We Will Rock You by Queen.

werk/eminem-the-marshall-mathers-lp.text:
After the success of The Slim Shady LP, Eminem had gone from underground rapper to celebrity, and he did not like it: he no longer trusted anyone. The third album was released on 23 May 2000. It was recorded in several studios around Detroit, with producers such as Dr. Dre, Mel-Man and F.B.T. The lyrics deal with his fame, the criticism of his music and the estrangement from his family. A trip to Amsterdam, with heavy drug use, made him decide to write openly about drugs.

The sound is hardcore and satirical hip hop with horrorcore. The Real Slim Shady, The Way I Am and Stan became singles; Stan is about an obsessed fan and gave the English language the word stan. The album caused a great stir through lyrics that were seen as violent, homophobic and misogynistic. Even so, it received positive reviews, and Rolling Stone named it the best album of 2000. It won a Grammy for Best Rap Album.
werk/eminem-the-marshall-mathers-lp.listen: Listen to Stan and notice how the story of an obsessed fan unfolds in the lyrics.

werk/eminem-the-marshall-mathers-lp-2.text:
The Marshall Mathers LP 2 is a sequel to Eminem's third album. The idea arose when, at an early stage, he recorded a handful of songs that reminded him of his earlier work. He wanted to experiment with retro sounds from turntablism, such as break beats and scratches, and asked Rick Rubin to take that further. Dr. Dre was executive producer.

The album draws on arena rock and old-school hip hop and sounds more minimalist than earlier records. Berzerk honours the hip hop of old with samples of the Beastie Boys and Billy Squier. In Rap God he raps over an instrumental with EDM influences and changing flows, and closes by asking why you would be king if you can be god. The Monster, with Rihanna, became an American number one. Critics praised the rapping skill and the production. The album won the Grammy for Best Rap Album.
werk/eminem-the-marshall-mathers-lp-2.listen: Listen to Rap God and notice how often and how quickly the flow of the rap changes.

werk/eminem-the-slim-shady-lp.text:
After the failure of his debut Infinite in 1996, Eminem invented the alter ego Slim Shady, whom he introduced in 1997 on the Slim Shady EP. At the Rap Olympics in Los Angeles he came second, and that brought him to Dr. Dre and Jimmy Iovine. The second album, from 1999, was recorded in Ferndale, Michigan. Dr. Dre often made a beat first, over which Eminem rapped loosely. The production was by Dr. Dre, the Bass Brothers and Eminem himself.

The beats are bass-heavy and recall West Coast hip hop. The lyrics, often told from the point of view of Slim Shady, contain cartoonish violence that, he said, was meant as a horror film. They also deal with poverty. My Name Is became his first entry in the Billboard Hot 100. Critics praised the fresh style and the black humour, and the record brought him two Grammys, although he was controversial for his lyrics.
werk/eminem-the-slim-shady-lp.listen: Listen to Guilty Conscience. Notice how Dr. Dre and Eminem, as angel and devil, influence the characters in the story.
